rows.verified: Commercial clients must appoint demolition contractors and designers with relevant skills, knowledge and experience.
The commercial client and principal designer must provide relevant pre-construction information to those who need it.
Principal designers must plan and manage health and safety during the pre-construction phase.
Principal contractors must plan and manage health and safety during demolition work.
Site managers must supervise workers and ensure safe working practices and plans are followed.
Alteration, demolition and dismantling must be planned and carried out by competent people to avoid unplanned structural collapse.
Dutyholders should remove the need for work at height where practicable, for example by using a high-reach machine with a protected cab.
Demolition planning must protect workers and the public and control dust, debris and uncontrolled-collapse risks.
Demolition risk depends on structural form, sequence, temporary support, site boundary, adjacent property, plant, competence and supervision.
HSE demolition evidence is structure-, site-, method-, contractor-, control- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level casualty probability.
The law requires danger to workers in or near excavations to be prevented.
A competent person must inspect excavation supports or battering at the start of the working shift and at specified times.
No work should take place in an excavation until it is safe.
Planning information should cover ground conditions, underground structures or watercourses and the location of existing services.
No ground can be relied upon to remain unsupported in all circumstances.
Depending on conditions, one cubic metre of soil can weigh more than 1.5 tonnes.
Excavations require safe access and egress; suitable ladders must be secure, on a firm base and normally extend at least one metre above the landing.
Excavations must also be inspected after events affecting stability, with faults corrected immediately and reports made where required.
Excavation risk depends on soil and water conditions, depth, support, nearby structures, services, plant movements, weather and inspection quality.
HSE excavation evidence is site-, ground-, support-, task-, worker- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collapse probability.
